metadata.case_name: WONG MAN LUNG JOEY v. LIU TSZ MING

plaintiff.occupation_before: Tourist bus driver for Union Tourist Rental Car Limited (from 9 January 2009 up to the time of the accident)

source: The provisional diagnosis was chest injury and analgesic drugs were prescribed.
the plaintiff was diagnosed as suffering from (i) chest injury, (ii) neck sprain, and (iii) back pain;
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of cervical spine

source: He was suffering from the symptoms of chest and back injuries.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of muscle, fascia or tendon of abdomen, lower back or pelvis, unspecified

source: On 10 April 2009, he attended the A&E Department of Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Hospital (“NH”) complaining of right shoulder and low back pain. On physical examination, he was diagnosed as suffering from joint pain in right shoulder and was treated and discharged on the same day.
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the shoulder or upper arm, unspecified

injuries.description: desiccation of C5/6, C6/7 discs with right posterolateral protrusion probably causing impingement on the right C6 nerve root
source: MRI of the cervical spine was performed showing desiccation of C5/6, C6/7 discs with right posterolateral protrusion probably causing impingement on the right C6 nerve root, no significant cervical cord compression.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of nerve root of cervical spine

source: The plaintiff had suffered from an adjustment disorder with depressed mood according to the DSM-IV diagnostic criteria. It was compatible that the adjustment disorder was caused by the accident.

manifestations.description: neck stiffness and pain on rotation
decreased neck rotation to the left
right upper limb weakness with muscle power grade 4+/5 in all myotomes
right C5 dermatome decreased light touch sensation
tenderness at paraspinal muscles and trapezius
occasional vague auditory hallucinations and seeing shadows (described as 'non-existing voices and shadows')

treatments_received: A&E attendance and analgesic medication (5 April 2009)
Physiotherapy (1st course: 17 April 2009 to 28 October 2009) - 33 sessions
Physiotherapy (2nd course: 22 January 2010 to 26 May 2010) - 18 sessions
Work hardening program / Occupational Therapy (16 October 2009 to 4 December 2009)
Pain clinic attendance and trigger point injection (29 April 2010)
Psychiatric outpatient treatment with medications (mirtazapine, quetiapine, diazepam, clonazepam, alprazolam) and regular psychiatric follow-up
treatments_future: Continuous psychiatric treatment required to optimize control of mood disorder
Drs opined psychiatric follow-up seemingly for a period of 1 to 2 years at an average interval of once in four weeks (public clinic)

losses.description: The plaintiff had suffered from an adjustment disorder with depressed mood according to the DSM-IV diagnostic criteria. It was compatible that the adjustment disorder was caused by the accident.
